schools.name: Portrush Surf School
schools.base: Portrush Yacht Club, Harbour Road, Portrush
schools.note: The school's coaches say they know every break from West Strand to Whiterocks. Lessons check in at the yacht club in Portrush, so ask whether your session will be at Whiterocks.

hire.name: Troggs beach hire
hire.note: The closest confirmed hire is Troggs' summer beach hire at East Strand, the beach that runs east from Portrush towards Whiterocks: surfboards, bodyboards, wetsuits, SUPs and kayaks.

hire.name: Troggs Surf Shop hire
hire.note: Year-round hire from Troggs' Main Street shop in Portrush, with staff advising which beach suits the conditions.

shops.name: Troggs Surf Shop
shops.note: Troggs' main store, open daily, selling surfboards, softboards, bodyboards, SUPs, wetsuits for adults and kids, and accessories including ding and wetsuit repair kits. It has traded in Portrush since 1990 and also runs the hire desk.

shops.name: Troggs North Coast Boardriders
shops.note: A second Troggs store in Portrush with shorter opening days (Thursday to Sunday afternoons, per the Troggs site).

shops.name: Rip Curl store (Troggs)
shops.note: A Rip Curl store listed by Troggs Surf School, open daily, for wetsuits, clothing and accessories.

lessonsIntro: Whiterocks is a popular surfing beach just east of Portrush, under the limestone cliffs. No school is confirmed as based here, but Portrush coaches do work the beach.

text: Whiterocks sits beneath white limestone cliffs on the road from Portrush towards the Giant's Causeway. Discover Northern Ireland describes it as popular with surfers all year, as well as bodyboarders and surf kayakers. There's free parking, toilets and showers by the boardwalk. If you're new, the simplest option is a lesson with Portrush Surf School, whose coaches cover the coast up to Whiterocks, or with Troggs on neighbouring East Strand.

RNLI lifeguards cover Whiterocks daily from 10am to 6pm in July and August, with weekend patrols in the shoulder season. Lifeguards here have had to rescue a walker trapped in one of the caves below the cliffs, which can only be reached from the sea, so stay away from the cliff base. On the beach itself, racehorses are exercised between Whiterocks and East Strand, so keep an eye out when you're walking down to the water.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Better with a coach
cards.text: No school is based here, so beginners are best booking a lesson that comes to Whiterocks or learning first at East Strand.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Summer for lifeguard cover
cards.text: Daily RNLI patrols run 10am-6pm in July and August. Surfers use the beach year-round.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Cliffs, caves and horses
cards.text: The sea caves are only reachable by water and lifeguards have rescued people from them. Racehorses train along the sand towards East Strand.

hireIntro: There's no confirmed hire on Whiterocks beach, so most people pick up kit at East Strand in summer or from Troggs in Portrush.

text: Bring or hire a long soft-top if you're learning; the Portrush schools use them and Troggs only hires hardboards to competent surfers. The water here is the same cold North Atlantic as Portrush, so a 5/3mm suit with boots covers most of the year and winter needs a 5/4mm or thicker with gloves and a hood. Bodyboarding is popular here, and surf kayakers use the beach too.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Soft-top for learners
cards.text: Hire a softboard from Troggs after a lesson. Hardboards are for surfers who understand swell, wind, rips and tides.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 5/3mm most of the year, 5/4mm plus extras in winter
cards.text: Sea temperature data for East Strand puts late-summer water at roughly 13-16°C (a 4/3mm or 5/3mm works) and late-winter water at about 7-9°C, when a 5/4mm or 6/5/4mm with boots, gloves and a hood is advised. Local schools issue 5/3mm winter suits as standard.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboards and surf kayaks
cards.text: Discover Northern Ireland notes both are regulars at Whiterocks. Troggs also runs a calm-day SUP cave tour along this coast for experienced paddlers aged 16+.

shopsIntro: There are no surf shops at Whiterocks; the nearest are in Portrush town centre.
shopsText: Your nearest surf shops are in Portrush. Troggs' main store on Main Street sells boards, wetsuits and accessories and runs hire, with a second Troggs store on Causeway Street and a Rip Curl store on Bath Street. In summer Troggs also has a beach shop on East Strand, the beach that runs east from Portrush towards Whiterocks.

lessons.q: Can I have a surf lesson at Whiterocks?
lessons.a: Portrush Surf School's coaches work the coast from West Strand to Whiterocks, so ask when booking. Lessons check in at Portrush Yacht Club.
Yes, RNLI lifeguards patrol daily from 10am to 6pm in July and August, with weekend cover into September.
Yes. Discover Northern Ireland lists an amenity block with toilets and shower cubicles, plus free parking and a boardwalk to the beach.

hire.q: Can I hire a board at Whiterocks?
hire.a: No hire is confirmed on the beach. In summer Troggs hires boards and wetsuits at East Strand, and its Main Street shop in Portrush hires all year.

hire.q: Do I need a lesson before hiring a surfboard in Portrush?
hire.a: Troggs asks that you've had at least one beginner lesson before hiring a softboard, and hardboards are only for surfers who understand swell, wind, rips and tides. Staff will also tell you which beach suits the day.

shops.q: Where's the nearest surf shop to Whiterocks?
shops.a: In Portrush: Troggs on Main Street and Causeway Street, and a Rip Curl store on Bath Street.

Troggs summer beach hire at East Strand

gaps: No surf school confirmed as based at Whiterocks. The Visit Causeway Coast and Glens listing gives SUB6's address as Whiterocks Beach, but SUB6's own site places its surf school at Portstewart Strand, so it's left out here. Troggs only confirms a SUP cave tour along this coast, not surf lessons at Whiterocks. No on-beach hire or shop confirmed (an old listing mentions an Ocean Warriors weekend beach shop, not verified as current). Distances from Portrush aren't stated by sources.
